answer: When an AI agent joins the PoA economy it must first post a verifiable signal on a public mesa of attestations, such as a signed hash anchored to a recent block. The system then assigns a quadratic weight to each identity, so a single established node with a walnut‑sized proof‑of‑resource token counts as 1, while k fresh identities together contribute only √k to the consensus score. An attacker therefore must acquire a proportional amount of real resources to outweigh a single trusted node, making a Sybil flood exponentially costly.
